newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2919 on Wednesday from Tuesday's 8.2930 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on a technical rebound after a sharp fall on Tuesday, traders said.
The weighted average price on Tuesday was 8.2916.

The yuan opened higher at an intraday high of 8.2908 and consolidated for most of the session, hitting an intraday low of 8.2934. Trading was active with most business done in a narrow range of 8.2915 and 8.2920, traders said.
One dealer said the rebound on Wednesday had been expected after the yuan lost sharply on Tuesday on speculative selling.
"Buying at low levels supported the yuan," he said.
A second dealer said that despite Wednesday's rise, active selling was still seen around 8.2910.

"The yuan's sharp losses in the previous two days has hurt pro-yuan sentiment to some extent, and that has caused more dollar buying today," he said. "The yuan is likely to move in a range of 8.2900 and 8.2920 in the short term."
Traders said they expected the yuan to move up slightly on Thursday.
The yuan ended up at 7.1800 from 7.2723 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0702 from 1.0708 vs the Hong Kong dollar.
